stem: A workload serves static website content with no need for a POSIX file interface, and the team wants the cheapest baseline storage service before adding any lifecycle policy.

choices.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

rationale: Amazon S3 has no capacity to provision and bills only for what is stored plus requests, making it the cheapest baseline for object data with no POSIX file interface requirement. FSx for Windows File Server carries a premium for a managed Windows/AD-native engine that this workload does not need. EFS has a higher per-GB rate than S3 and exists to provide a POSIX file interface, which the workload does not require. EBS bills for provisioned capacity whether or not it is used and has to be attached to a single instance, which does not fit shared static content at the cheapest baseline cost.
